13.0.0.en: After Christ's talk mentioned in the previous chapter, some asked Him about Pilate, the governor of Judea, that is, the southern part of Palestine, and how he killed the Galilaeans, the inhabitants of its northern part, who were known for causing many disturbances. They had risen in a revolt calling for not submitting to Caesar, and it seems they were followers of Judas of Galilee (Acts 5:37). Pilate sent his soldiers to them while they were in the temple offering their sacrifices, and he killed them and mingled their blood with their sacrifices.

13.1.0.en: It seems there was a disagreement between the Pharisees, who did not incline to using violence against the authorities, and the sect of the Zealots, who did incline to it, and they differed in their judgment of this incident. The Pharisees considered them wicked men who deserved punishment, while the Zealots rose up against Pilate's unjust violence. Some thought that these Galilaeans were more wicked than the rest of the people, because God allowed them to be killed while they were offering their sacrifices in the temple, that is, He did not accept them. In addition, there was a common thought at that time that whoever is struck by a calamity suffers it because of his wickedness, and whoever is not struck is righteous. This is of course a mistaken thought, because God allows afflictions for His children in order to develop them spiritually, and He may give blessings to sinners in order to save them so that they repent.

13.2.0.en: Christ denied that the killing was a result of their sins being greater than those of others; truly they were sinners like others, but Christ called everyone to repentance, using this incident as a warning.

13.2.1.en: Not every sin has an earthly punishment, nor does a more severe earthly punishment mean the gravity of the sin. But may it be that when we hear of an affliction or meet one, it leads us to repentance, so that we are saved, not from temporal afflictions but rather from eternal torment.

13.3.0.en: Christ mentioned an incident that seems to have been recent and to have happened in Jerusalem, namely the fall of a tower upon a group of people who were in it, and eighteen of them died.

13.3.1.en: This was an affliction not caused by man, and He asked: were these Jews, do you suppose, more wicked than the rest of the Jews?

13.4.0.en: Christ answered His question in the negative, declaring that all are sinners, and that these incidents should call them to repentance and to preparing for eternity.

13.4.1.en: May we always prepare by repentance when we hear of any afflictions that befall others or of some falling into sins, and may we not judge them.

13.5.s.en: (2) The parable of the barren fig tree

13.5.0.en: "A certain man": He is God, the owner of the vineyard.

13.5.2.en: The fig tree represents the life of man.

13.5.3.en: The fruit is worship and good works.

13.5.4.en: Fruit trees are planted for the sake of their fruit, and if they bring no fruit they are of no use; likewise God created man to do good works, and if he has no such fruit there is no benefit in his existence in life.

13.6.0.en: "Seeking fruit": this means God's repeated asking of fruit from us. He always waits for it and comes to us through His warnings in the Holy Bible, through spiritual sermons, and through the virtues of those around us, which should move us to imitate them.

13.6.1.en: God was patient with the tree for three years, a long period, and it gave no fruit, so it deserved to be cut down, lest it draw nourishment and occupy a place to no purpose.

13.6.2.en: The first year signifies the life of humanity after the Fall, the second year is the age of the fathers Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, and the third year is the age of the Law and the prophets.

13.6.3.en: In all this humanity was not saved from sin, and did not give the response of love that is required toward God.

13.6.4.en: Do not make light of God's longsuffering toward you, but seize the opportunity for repentance and good works, lest you destroy your life.

13.7.0.en: The vinedresser is Christ, who intercedes for humanity, and he also signifies the priest and the servant who care for souls, call them to repentance and help them with the means of grace.

13.7.1.en: "Let it alone this year also": signifies the era of grace, in which the soul believes and is saved, and it also signifies the rest of the life that it lives, for this is its opportunity for repentance.

13.7.2.en: "Dig about it": that is, dig around the tree to pull out the weeds and get rid of harmful insects. This signifies repentance and humility with all their striving, because the digging goes deep downward like humility, and examining the soil and cutting the weeds is the review of the soul through repentance and confession.

13.7.3.en: "Dung": this is the fertilizer given to the tree, which signifies spiritual food by being nourished through Holy Communion, reading the Holy Bible and prayers.

13.8.0.en: Christ's hope in you is that you bear fruit, like the vinedresser's hope in the fig tree. If you disappoint His hope, nothing awaits you but being cut down, that is, death, and then what is more than this, that is, going to eternal torment. Remember, as long as you are alive, that God loves you and expects fruit from you and helps you if you obey His commandments.

13.9.s.en: (3) The healing of the bent woman

13.9.0.en: The temple was in Jerusalem, but the synagogues were spread throughout the land, where the Holy Scriptures were read and interpreted. Christ entered one of these synagogues on the Sabbath day, and it seems that the people expected Him to come to it, so some sick people came for Him to heal them and to hear His teachings, because He used to teach in these synagogues, since He came to fulfill the Law and the prophets.

13.10.0.en: A woman came to the synagogue who was afflicted with an illness that had bent her back for eighteen years, and this was from an unclean spirit (a spirit of infirmity), that is, the work of Satan, which made her look at the ground like animals, and not stand upright looking to heaven like other people.

13.10.1.en: The number ten signifies the commandments and the Law, and the number eight points to the Resurrection, which took place on the eighth day. So when the Law was completed with the Resurrection, that is, when eighteen years had passed, Christ healed her; that is, it is by Christ that the healing of humanity and its freedom from the authority of the devil is accomplished.

13.11.0.en: Christ commanded her by His word, that is, with the authority of His divinity, and she was loosed from her infirmity and her bending, and was freed from the authority of Satan, after He touched her with His hand, so she was healed immediately and praised God and glorified Him.

13.12.0.en: The ruler of the Jewish synagogue was indignant because he envied Christ, since hearts were attached to Him after this miracle, and he hid his envy under the cover of his adherence to the law of not working on the Sabbath, considering healing to be the work of a physician. And fearing to speak to Christ, he rebuked the people and told them to come to be healed on a day other than the Sabbath, although the woman had not asked Christ to heal her; rather it was He, in His love, who called her.

13.13.0.en: Christ rebuked the ruler of the synagogue for his hypocrisy, for he was not concerned about the Sabbath but envied Christ because of the people's love for Him; and healing is a miracle and not a work that violates the law.

13.13.1.en: And Christ gave a proof of this by which He put to shame the ruler of the synagogue and those with him of the Pharisees: that the law allows necessary works on the Sabbath day, such as loosing animals and taking them to water them.

13.14.0.en: All the more this Jewish woman, over whom Satan had held sway for eighteen years with the illness of bending, ought to be loosed on the Sabbath day, because this is a necessary need, and she is of course better than the animals. If an animal is tied up for the night only and we pity it for thirst and give it water, how much more does this woman, a daughter of Abraham, that is, a Jewess of the people of God, deserve mercy after Satan had bound her for 18 years and wearied her greatly.

13.15.0.en: The obstinate ones who were with the ruler of the synagogue were ashamed, and the crowds rejoiced at the miracles of Christ in healing them.

13.15.1.en: Do not be biased in your speech with people, but rejoice in the doing of good by any person and in every place.

13.16.s.en: (4) The parables of the mustard seed and the leaven

13.16.0.en: He likens the Kingdom of God to a grain of mustard seed, which is a very small seed that, when cast into the ground and buried, comes up as a great tree. So the Church began small in Judea and then spread throughout the whole world. A person must be buried like a mustard seed, to rise with Christ as a great tree in which the birds of the air lodge, that is, all the spiritual people who praise God attach themselves to the believer.

13.17.0.en: After Christ gave a parable close to the minds of farmers, He gave another parable that women who make bread understand easily, namely putting leaven into flour, so that it ferments as the leaven spreads through all the dough, and it becomes fit to be made into bread.

13.17.1.en: So the word of God works within the soul, and "three" points to the body, soul and spirit. The leaven is the proclamation that has spread throughout the whole world, because the world came out of three, the sons of Noah, and the leaven is the proclamation of the Holy Trinity, which has become spiritual food for all the children of God.

13.17.2.en: Do not despise your weakness, for God is able to work through you so that you influence many, and your prayer and your reading, however little, will change your life. Persevere in holding fast to God and in serving Him.

13.18.0.en: Christ headed toward Jerusalem, where He would be crucified by the Jews for the redemption of humanity, and He taught in the cities and villages through which He passed, calling them to repentance and preparing them to bear the cross in readiness for the Kingdom.

13.19.0.en: One of the crowd asked Him about the number of those who reach the Kingdom, and He did not answer him, because it is a theoretical question that does not benefit the salvation of the soul. Then He directed the hearers' attention to how to be saved and reach the Kingdom, namely by spiritual striving, which He expressed as entering by the narrow door, which means bowing down, humility and detachment from material attachments so that we can pass through it. And He made clear that many will seek to enter by it and will not be able, because of their clinging to material desires and pride and their unreadiness for continual striving in prayers and fasts, bearing with others, and laboring in serving them.

13.20.0.en: He likens God to the master of the house who shuts this narrow door leading to the Kingdom, and this is what happens at the end of a person's life. After this, people try to enter, and God refuses, declaring that He does not know them, that is, that they are not His children, because they preferred the love of the world to the love of Him, and were careless about holding to His commandments, delaying until their lives ended.

13.21.0.en: The wicked reply and say that we had a relationship with You in our lives, O God, in our daily living (eating and drinking), and we heard Your teaching (You taught in our streets). These had an outward relationship in spiritual practices but without depth and without true love from the heart.

13.22.0.en: God affirms that He does not know these wicked ones, and asks them "whence you are," that is, that you are not My children but the children of the devil. He reminds them of their evils and of their wronging of others and of themselves by neglecting their salvation, as they walked in the way of sin, and He rebukes them to depart from Him and go to eternal torment.

13.23.0.en: He describes eternal torment as having in it severe grief, one of whose manifestations is weeping, and also terror and torment that no one can imagine, which is signified by the gnashing of teeth.

13.23.1.en: On the other side, in the Kingdom, sit the fathers Abraham, Isaac and Jacob and also the prophets whom the Jews know, in joy and rejoicing. The wicked Jews who refused to believe in Christ and to walk spiritually look at them and cannot enter to them, and they see with them many believers of Gentile origin who come from the whole world, that is, from the east and the west, and rejoice with the fathers and the prophets in the Kingdom.

13.24.0.en: Christ declares to His hearers who refuse to believe in Him that those who thought themselves first to enter the Kingdom, such as the Jews, will be far away in eternal torment because of their unbelief in Christ, and the others, such as the Gentiles or the simple Jews who believed in Christ, will be first to enter the Kingdom and enjoy being with God and the saints.

13.24.1.en: If you bear toils in striving and fight your desires, holding fast to Christ, God will raise you up and give you a leading place in the Kingdom.

13.25.0.en: Herod is Herod Antipas, the governor appointed by the Romans over Galilee and also Perea, where Christ was preaching at that time. He is the one who killed John the Baptist, and it was to him that Pilate sent Christ bound to be tried.

13.25.1.en: The Pharisees envied Christ because of the people's love for Him, and it seems they stirred up Herod against Him and frightened him with Christ's popularity and power, so they got from him a word that Christ should leave Jerusalem, so that Herod could be rid of Him without causing a disturbance and troubles among the people. The Pharisees pretended to love Christ and to want to protect His life from Herod's violence, but they were deceivers who wanted to be rid of Christ.

13.26.0.en: Christ likened Herod Antipas to a fox, for he is deceitful and hard of heart, and declared that He did not fear him, sending with the Pharisees a strong message to him that He would continue His care for His people by casting out demons and healing the sick until He completed His work of redemption, announcing His resurrection on the third day.

13.26.1.en: The expression "today and tomorrow, and the third day I shall be perfected" was a well-known expression among the Jews, meant to indicate a short period; that is, the three days point to the nearness of the end of His preaching.

13.27.0.en: "Today and tomorrow" and what follows do not mean a few days, but the period in which He preaches, which is short because the completion of the redemption has drawn near.

13.27.1.en: "It cannot be that a prophet perish out of Jerusalem", where the Sanhedrin sits, the supreme Jewish council which unjustly judges the prophets and kills them, or judges Christ and crucifies Him?? This saying does not mean all the prophets, but most of them perish in Jerusalem.

13.27.2.en: Christ confirms His continuing in the care of His people until He dies in Jerusalem, which destroyed many of the prophets sent by Him.

13.28.1.en: Christ reproaches Jerusalem, that is, the Jews who dwell in it, because of their great shedding of the blood of the prophets, and declares His love for it throughout history and until now, and His attempt to gather its children and care for them with His love, as a hen lovingly gathers her chicks under her wings because of their weakness and their need for warmth; but sadly the Jews refused to listen to God's word and to believe in Him.

13.28.2.en: God's grace is ready to save you from all your troubles and sins, so respond to it and enjoy God's embrace.

13.29.0.en: "Ye shall not see me": because Christ will die and rise and ascend to heaven, and they will not see Him going about preaching among them after that.

13.29.1.en: "Blessed is he that cometh in the name of the Lord": a prophecy from Christ that of the Jews who refuse to believe in Him, some will afterward believe and declare their faith that Jesus is the awaited Messiah, blessed by God, who comes from heaven in the name of the Lord for the salvation of the world.

13.29.2.en: Christ declares the regrettable truth, which is the desolation of Jerusalem because of its pride, its stubbornness and its unbelief, that perhaps the Jews may return and believe.

13.29.3.en: And another truth: the Jews' unbelief that He is the Christ the Saviour; but a time will come when the rest of the Jews will believe and declare their faith, saying, "Blessed is he that cometh in the name of the Lord."

13.29.4.en: The healing of the man with dropsy. The last place at the table. Like the supper of the lord, and counting the cost. The healing of the man with dropsy (vv. 1-6):

13.29.5.en: 1- And it came to pass, as he went into the house of one of the chief Pharisees to eat bread on the sabbath day, that they watched him. 2- And, behold, there was a certain man before him which had the dropsy. 3- And Jesus answering spake unto the lawyers and Pharisees, saying, "Is it lawful to heal on the sabbath day? 4- "And they held their peace. And he took him, and healed him, and let him go; 5- And answered them, and said, "Which of you shall have an ass or an ox fallen into a pit, and will not straightway pull him out on the sabbath day? 6- "And they could not answer him again to these things.
